case_title: AMIR HAMZA SHAIKH & ORS. v. STATE OF MAHARASHTRA & ANR.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.27
neutral_facts: The case involves a dispute over the permission to conduct prosecution. The accused were denied permission to prosecute by the trial court, but the High Court granted permission to the complainant to proceed with the prosecution. The matter was remitted back to the Magistrate to reconsider whether the complainant should be granted permission to prosecute the offences under Sections 498-A, 406 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code. The judgment discusses the legal principles regarding the rights of victims and the role of the Magistrate in granting permission for prosecution. The case does not involve any specific incident, evidence, or details about the accused or the victim beyond the procedural aspects of the prosecution.
